svg.title: Data Modelling in Microsoft Fabric: From Raw Sources to Star Schema to Semantic Model
svg.desc: An architecture diagram tracing data modelling from source systems through a medallion lakehouse into a dimensional gold layer and up into a Power BI semantic model. Source systems land in a Bronze lakehouse layer unchanged. A Silver layer cleanses and conforms that data; an inference callout notes that teams needing full historical traceability sometimes insert a data-vault-style raw staging structure (hubs, links, satellites) at this point, though Fabric has no dedicated data-vault product feature. From Silver, a fixed ETL order — stage, then dimensions, then facts, then post-processing — loads a Gold-layer dimensional model built as a star schema: dimension tables radiating around central fact tables, built either as a Warehouse or as Lakehouse materialized views. A dimension-table detail node explains surrogate keys and slowly changing dimension handling; a fact-table detail node explains grain, foreign keys to dimension surrogate keys, and the practitioner heuristic that a fact table with more than roughly 50 columns is usually hiding a dimension. The star schema feeds a Direct Lake semantic model, which can build a composite model keeping large fact tables in Direct Lake mode while smaller dimension tables use Import or DirectQuery. Two warning nodes flag real failure modes: applying row-level security at the Warehouse T-SQL layer forces Direct Lake semantic models built on that table into DirectQuery fallback, and Fabric Warehouse does not enforce foreign keys, so referential integrity between fact and dimension surrogate keys is the ETL process's responsibility, not the database's.
svg.text: From raw sources through medallion staging to a star-schema Gold layer and a Direct Lake composite semantic model

g.title: Source systems — Operational databases, SaaS APIs, files, and events that carry the raw data a dimensional model will eventually describe.
Bronze layer (Lakehouse) — Raw data stored exactly as received, with no transformation, inside a Fabric Lakehouse.
g.text: No transformation; ideally landed via a OneLake shortcut,
not a physical copy, so it stays fully replayable.

g.title: Silver layer (cleansed) — Errors fixed, formats standardized, duplicates removed — data conformed but not yet dimensionally modelled.
g.text: Errors fixed, formats standardized, duplicates removed;
valid staging source for the dimensional ETL below.

g.title: Data vault staging (optional pattern) — Hub/link/satellite modelling as an architectural option for teams needing full historical auditability before dimensional modelling. Fabric Atlas architectural interpretation, not a documented Microsoft Fabric feature.

g.aria-label: Dimensional ETL: stage, dimensions, facts, post-process
g.title: Dimensional ETL: stage → dimensions → facts → post-process — A fixed load order: staging tables, then dimension tables, then fact tables, then post-processing such as semantic-model refresh.
g.text: Surrogate keys must exist before facts reference them — order is a hard dependency, not style.

g.aria-label: Gold layer: star schema (dimensions and facts)
g.title: Gold layer: star schema (dimensions + facts) — A central fact table surrounded by dimension tables, Microsoft's recommended default design for a Fabric Warehouse.
g.text: multiple fact tables can form multiple stars

g.aria-label: Dimension table: surrogate keys and slowly changing dimension handling
g.title: Dimension table: surrogate keys + SCD — Business entities with a surrogate key and slowly changing dimension (SCD) history handling.
g.text: is the join target for facts.

g.aria-label: Fact table: grain and foreign keys
g.title: Fact table: grain + foreign keys — Measurable events at one consistent grain, referencing dimension surrogate keys — with no enforced foreign keys in Fabric Warehouse.

g.aria-label: Warning: no enforced foreign keys in Fabric Warehouse
g.title: Warning: no enforced foreign keys in Warehouse — Fabric Warehouse does not enforce foreign key constraints, so fact-to-dimension referential integrity is the ETL's job.
g.text: No enforced foreign keys in Warehouse
ETL must check fact→dimension key integrity itself;
failed lookups route to an "Unknown" member, not a dropped row.

g.title: Semantic model (Direct Lake composite) — A Power BI semantic model reading the star schema directly from OneLake via Direct Lake, with large fact tables in Direct Lake and small dimensions optionally in Import mode.

svg.text: reports · DAX queries · Analyze in Excel

g.aria-label: Warning: row-level security at the wrong layer breaks Direct Lake
g.title: Warning: RLS at the wrong layer breaks Direct Lake — T-SQL row-level security on a Warehouse table forces dependent Direct Lake semantic models into DirectQuery fallback.

svg.text: inference — Fabric Atlas interpretation, not a product feature
Vendored official Fabric icons: Lakehouse, Dataflow Gen2, Semantic model, OneLake, Power BI — used unchanged with adjacent product labels, per docs/official-icon-policy.md.
Fabric Atlas — original diagram, July 2026. Not a Microsoft asset; palette from the official Fabric icon.
